newsitem.title: UK: NWE low sulphur cracked fuel at post-Gulf War high.
newsitem.headline: NWE low sulphur cracked fuel at post-Gulf War high.

text.p: NWE low sulphur cracked fuel oil rallied to its highest point on Thursday since the winter of 1991 when oil prices peaked because of the Gulf War.
Knocked higher by cold weather on the eastern seaboard of the United States, thinner supplies in Europe and tight shipping tonnage low sulphur prices have plenty of upwards potential.
"Even if crude goes down we expect low sulphur to stay flat to catch up for its usual seasonal advantage," said a trader at a European major.
Physical low sulphur cargoes were pegged around $129-130 fob NWE on Thursday, having risen from a touch below $120 this time last week.
The spread between low sulphur and Brent front month crude stood around $3.63 a barrel on Wednesday compared with $1.40 this time last year.
"The spread we have is a summer spread, not close to the winter level," said one dealer. During this summer the spread was around $3.00.

The bullish impetus of the cold weather in the eastern United States, which has made gas expensive compared with fuel and generated a buying spree on fuel, is supported by the fundamental tightness in the European market. U.S. fuel will be encouraged to meet local demand and not head transatlantic to cover demand from the world's largest buyer, Italian state oil company Enel.
"Anyone hoping for large amounts of Caribbean product will be disappointed," said a trader.
After a spate of deals this week only one large 40-50,000 tonne cargo remains available for November loading.
November and December paper traded on Thursday at $129.25 fob NWE while January swaps were put at $129-130.
